finding.name: organizations/550178366891/sources/3913548688797809695/locations/global/findings/b54fa158d3244cdf9b6ffeacefaa9ec6
finding.category: Privilege Escalation: Launch of privileged Kubernetes container
finding.description:
A potentially malicious actor created a Pod that contains privileged containers (`privileged` field set to `true`) or containers with privilege escalation capabilities (`allowPrivilegeEscalation` field set to `true`).

Privileged containers allow nearly unrestricted host access. They share namespaces with the host, and lack control group, seccomp, AppArmor, and capability restrictions.

Containers with privilege escalation capabilities allow a process created within the container to execute a set-user-id, set-group-id, or file capability executable to gain the privileges specified by the executable. The lack of preventive security control increases the risk of container escape.

**Recommended action**

1. Confirm that the container created requires access to host resources and kernel capabilities.
1. Determine whether there are other signs of malicious activity by the principal in the logs.
1. If the principal email isn't a service account, contact the owner of the account to confirm whether the legitimate owner conducted the action.
1. If the principal email is a service account (IAM or Kubernetes), identify the source of the action to determine its legitimacy.

[More details](https://cloud.google.com/security-command-center/docs/findings/threats/gke-control-plane-launch-privileged-container)
